Context: Josephine and her brother Angelo have traveled through a snowstorm to see the famous P. T. Barnum circus. Josephine has always wanted to meet P. T. Barnum.
Title: Passage 2: Meeting Mr. Barnum
Author: by Patricia Baehr
Content: In the storm, the `text(two)` blocks to `text(Fourth)` Avenue and `text(Twenty-fourth)` Street felt like `text(miles)`. But at last Josephine saw a poster, cleared of ice, with the image of a large balding head with waves of hair as white as snow — Mr. P. T. Barnum himself. . . .

Madison Square Garden was the biggest building Josephine had ever seen. A smiling man with a droopy mustache showed her and Angelo where to go inside. He didn’t check their tickets for seat numbers but led them straight to the front row, where they had a perfect view of `text(three)` rings surrounded by a track. Though Josephine had heard the Garden had room for `text(twelve thousand)` people, there were hardly more present than had been on the `ultext(el car)`. She rubbed herself to get warm while listening to strange echoes made by more than a `text(hundred)` shovels scraping snow off the roof. If she had any fears about whether the show would go on, they disappeared when the band started playing. The music was loud enough to drown out the sound of the shovels and the memory of the storm as well.

It was announced that all `text(eighty-six)` acts would appear that `text(day)`. Acrobats on high wires. The Siegrists, a family of gymnasts. Brave men taming big, ferocious cats. Elephants — Totonno’s long-nosed animals — doing tricks. Costumed bears dancing, and a goat riding atop a galloping horse. There was a little girl named Flora Stirk who rode a bicycle and juggled. Then a lady with “moss hair” charmed a snake, and Madame Eliza Dockrill, the “Empress of the Arena,” displayed her amazing skills on the back of a horse. Finally, Zazel the Human Cannonball exploded from the mouth of a canon, and ostriches and camels raced around the track with monkeys on their backs.

Nothing excited Josephine more, though, than the sight of a carriage rolling into the `ultext(arena)`. When it stopped in the center ring, everything grew still. Josephine held her breath as [a] man in a suit and vest stood up to speak in a voice that was strong and clear.
“You came to see Barnum? Well, I’m Barnum. The storm may be a great show, but I still have the greatest show on earth!”
As the horse trotted out to the track, Josephine cheered so loudly that she hurt her throat. To her amazement, the carriage stopped directly in front of her.
“Are you having a good time?” Mr. Barnum asked, leaning down to shake Angelo’s and Josephine’s hands.
There she was: face to face with Mr. P. T. Barnum! Finally she could ask how he had made his fortunes! At last, she would know how to succeed in America — if only she could speak!
Angelo poked her hard in the ribs as the carriage pulled away to deposit Mr. Barnum in his special box seat. “Think what we went through,” he `ultext(jeered)`, “and you say nothing!”

Josephine leaned back and tried to forget her shame as the circus continued. Her gaze kept shifting to Mr. Barnum, though. He roared with delight and seemed to enjoy everything as much as if it were his `text(first)` time at the circus, too. . . .
At the end of the show, Papa was outside waiting to see Josephine and Angelo home. . . .
Papa shook his head. “Only you and Mr. Ba dernum would think to go out on a `text(day)` like today, Josephine. Only you and Mr. Barnum.”

:box:`bbtext(Glossary)`

`ultext(el car)`: passenger section of a public subway train in New York City

`ultext(arena)`: a large central area that is surrounded by seats for viewers

`ultext(jeered)`: teased
